punchline: A computer beat Kasparov, but later even the strongest computer was beaten by human teams working with ordinary computers.
thirty_sec: In 1997 a computer beat the chess champion Kasparov. David Epstein does not read this as the end of human intelligence: chess is a kind world with clear rules, while real life is blurry and uncertain. In the advanced chess Kasparov proposed, even the strongest computer was beaten by broad-minded human teams using ordinary computers. The human brought the context and strategy that the machine could not see.
